Imagine you threw away your nail clippers forever.
Most people think nails just sit there, like little shields.
But they're growing right now, pushed out from a root hidden under your skin.
New cells fill with keratin, the same tough stuff as hair, then die and slide forward.
Skip trimming for a year, and they'd stick out half as long as your fingers.
And they wouldn't grow straight. They'd curl and twist into spirals.
They'd turn heavy and brittle, and picking up a cup would be a struggle.
If they never snapped, after a lifetime each nail could be longer than you are tall.
So that little click of the clippers? It's keeping your hands working.
